shadows.notes: Chin/jaw shadow on neck and the collar-bone area of the body, light from upper right so the shadow falls down-left. It was baked into the neck and body skin; the baked part was removed by per-channel inverse multiply (lit skin neck (249,204,180), body (248,205,183)) and redone as one independent multiply layer, colour basis = reference shadow tone neck (221,163,144) / body (223,166,146), constant colour about (226,205,203) with the shadow fraction stored in alpha. Neck and body share one joint clip base (group 'receivers: neck + body') so the shadow is a single connected shape across both receivers. The layer is wider than the visible shadow (about 14 px diffusion margin past the visible edge, extends under the face/jaw) so the occluded part and motion margin remain.

Upper eyelid / lash shadow on the left eye (image left side is the character's right; this is eye_left). Follows the upper eyelid contour, not the iris gaze. The baked lid shadow on the sclera was restored to lit white (252,246,246) and redone as a multiply layer, colour basis = reference sclera shadow (198,186,192), constant colour about (203,195,201). Pixels on the pink shadow-edge tint were repainted to the lit base and carry that tint as per-pixel shadow colour/alpha, so the composite is unchanged. The iris previously had no lid shadow: a new crescent (strength 0.7, about 4 px deep following the lid) darkens the iris top edge only; iris shading, eyeliner and highlight are untouched. The shadow layer extends about 12 px beyond the eyelid contour (hidden by the opening mask and eyelid) as motion margin. Receivers are sclera and iris inside the 'eye_left globe' clip group, so the shadow is clipped to the eyeball.

Upper eyelid / lash shadow on the right eye. Same treatment as the left eye: baked sclera lid shadow restored to lit white (246,240,240) and redone as a multiply layer, colour basis = reference sclera shadow (198,192,210), constant colour about (205,204,223), pink shadow-edge pixels carried by per-pixel shadow colour/alpha; new iris-top crescent (strength 0.7, about 4 px deep) following the eyelid; about 12 px margin beyond the eyelid contour; clipped to the 'eye_right globe' group (sclera + iris).

Shadow of the T-shirt hem on the front of the shorts, light from upper right so it falls straight down below the hem curve. In the reference it was a baked dark band 1-9 px thick along the hem (thicker near the centre). The baked band was removed from the shorts front by per-channel inverse multiply (lit navy (60,73,104), shadow tone (44,54,79)) and redone as one independent multiply layer, ratio (0.733,0.740,0.760), constant colour about (187,189,194) with the shadow fraction stored in alpha. The same navy tone is used by the intrinsic fold wedges, the pleat lines and the dark side panels of the shorts; those were left baked in the shorts art (band thickness is capped by a smoothed value so the wedges stay baked below it, and the two side-panel columns are untouched). The shadow layer also extends 14 px upward under the shirt (occluded, so the hem can move) and is extrapolated sideways past the shorts silhouette as motion margin; the base layer's hidden dark pixels under the shirt were restored to lit navy so the moved shadow does not double-darken. Receiver is the shorts waist_crotch front layer itself, which is the clip base inside the isolated group 'shadow group: shirt hem on shorts'.

excluded.reason: No evidence of a cast shadow in the reference. Forehead skin stays flat (about (251,208,187)) from 4 to 12 px away from the bangs edges, with no darker band under the strands, including the long centre strand. The tan bands beside the brows and above the eyelids are the brow-bone/eyelid-fold shading belonging to the face art, not a hair shadow, and are kept as is. The 1-3 px fringe next to hair is outline anti-aliasing (pink tint), not darkening. Not drawn.

No evidence. Skin next to the side hair and at the temples is uniform up to the hair outline, and the ears show no darkening where the hair passes over them; their darker concha tone is the ear's own shading (kept). Not drawn.

excluded.reason: The thin outer tips lie over transparent background or the outline of the head, with no receiving skin region behind them showing a shadow. Outer hair outlines are not moved inward as shadow lines. Not drawn, so no fine-hair offsets are tested.

Back hair sits behind the head and neck; light from the upper right and a frontal view give no visible cast onto the neck beyond what is already covered by the chin shadow, and the reference shows none. Not drawn.
Ears sit on the face contour edge; the cheek next to the ears is flat in the reference, so no cast shadow exists to separate. Not drawn.

Thigh skin immediately under the shorts hem is already the lit tone ((248,206,184) from the first row below the hem), with no shadow band. The darker strips along the inner thighs are the leg's own shading and are kept. Not drawn.
No darker band follows the collar edge on the skin; the only shadow on the neck/chest skin is the chin shadow, handled as chin-to-neck-body. The collarbone marks are intrinsic shading. Not drawn.
